clusters.attribution: Both PRs are steipete/Peter Steinberger contributions. They are newly merged in this window, proposed earlier. Public-project work does not establish an employer research roadmap.
source_facts: #173873 adds durable operatorRecoverySource evidence with canonical bounded65,536-byte decoding, tied to requester agent/session/incarnation/lifecycle/sourceRun; snapshot scopes are bounded by admitted scopes.

Recovery evidence does not itself confer execution authority. Gateway owner restoration verifies stored/current requester identity and current policy/grant through restoreGatewayOperatorSource, with current owner/Gateway/lifecycle checks across awaits and no system fallback for missing or revoked evidence.
Restoration first restricts the row. Only overloaded WorkerTaskError re-arms the retry marker; successful restore or permanent refusal clears it. A revoked source is not a transient retry.
The selected exact-merge state code advances24->25 as a metadata-only compatibility fence for older readers. This does not assert latest-main schema is25; other commits may subsequently change it.

#173924 puts unattended recovery on dedicated RestartRecovery command lane, default concurrency4; visible demand-triggered recovery remains Main. It globally orders claimed candidates by endedAt or updatedAt with storePath/sessionKey ties, while keeping per-session serialization and existing ownership/admission deadlines.

Candidate preparation failure increments failed and continues to healthy candidates without clearing the failed interruption claim; abort still propagates. Maintenance waits for RestartRecovery queue. Four long-running recoveries can occupy all slots and backlog still progresses in waves.

Changed tests include8sessions/twostores FIFO, blocked background plus live Main control, startup/preparation capacity retry without charging/clearing marks, repeated interruption, and a Gateway-process fixture extended to5interrupted sessions with peak4 held provider responses and fifth starting after release.
